accepted.title: Cut-involution edge transitivity implies a graph norm
accepted.text: Let H be a finite connected simple bipartite graph with at least one edge. For a bounded real symmetric measurable function f on [0,1]², put t_H(|f|)=∫_[0,1]^{V(H)} ∏_{uv∈E(H)}|f(x_u,x_v)| ∏_{v∈V(H)}dx_v. Call H weakly norming if f↦t_H(|f|)^(1/|E(H)|) is a norm on this vector space modulo equality almost everywhere. A cut involution is a graph automorphism σ with σ²=id whose fixed vertices F separate H and for which V(H)∖F splits into nonempty sets L,R with no edges between them and σ(L)=R. Let W_H be the subgroup of Aut(H) generated by all cut involutions. If W_H acts transitively on E(H), must H be weakly norming?
accepted.subject: Combinatorics & Graph Theory
accepted.citation: Conjecture 6.42, printed p. 117 / held PDF p. 125; cut-involution domain and definition at printed p. 83 / PDF p. 91.
accepted.scope_review: Actual held physical pages 15,86,91–93,96–97,125–126 read. Connectedness is the standing domain of the cut-involution definition at physical91, not an invented percolation assumption. Functions remain symmetric real bounded measurable functions on the single square, rather than arbitrary nonsymmetric bigraph kernels. All cut involutions are allowed; edge transitivity alone does not assume a percolating sequence. Null functions are identified almost everywhere for the norm.
accepted.literature_finding: Coregliano 2408.14257 retains the stronger cut-percolation conjecture and characterizes percolation by absence of nonmonochromatic fold-stable colorings. That extra condition is not implied by its theorem from edge transitivity alone. Sidorenko’s ordinary automorphism-edge-transitivity necessity is also weaker than this source cut-group sufficiency target. No exact sufficiency proof or counterexample was verified in the dated bounded primary scan.
accepted.duplicate_review: Whole live catalog family search for graph norm/cut involution found no earlier target. Existing Banach-space norming/renorming questions concern different vector spaces and predicates. Independent full word/character/source-alias retrieval is required before numbering.
